get.summary: Report that the API is serving
How the web screen signs people in
List the workspaces the caller can reach
get.description: Owners and admins, and the owner token, see every workspace of the organisation; a member sees the workspaces assigned to them. Sorted by id.

get.summary: List the members assigned to a candidate record
get.description: Owners and admins read any record's members; a member reads those of a record assigned to them. Oldest assignment first.

put.summary: Assign a member to a candidate record
put.description: Owners and admins only. Assigning a member again returns the existing assignment.

delete.summary: Remove a member from a candidate record
delete.description: Owners and admins only. The member loses access to the record at once.

Removes the record for good: its stored files and exports, then its history, settings, consent ledger, audit trail, assignments and the knowledge bases it owns. Owners and admins only, or the owner token in owner-token mode, with the workspace id typed back as `confirm` (400 `confirmation_mismatch`). A queued or running run answers 409 `run_active`; stop it first. The record is missing to every other route from the first call, and calling again finishes an interrupted erasure.

confirm.description: The workspace id again, typed back by the person.

put.description: Creates the workspace with its language, models, run limits and execution mode. Only Anthropic and OpenAI models are routed by the hosted service; a side left out gets the default preset of `GET /v1/model-catalog` (Claude Sonnet as the author). An existing workspace is never overwritten: creating it again answers 409. In sign-in mode each workspace is a candidate record and takes one of the plan's record slots: 409 plan_limit_reached (limit candidateRecords) when none is left, 403 plan_required when the organisation has no plan.

get.summary: Read a workspace's configuration
Read the record's injection screening status
get.description: The latest screening status of each job source of the record's briefs and of each current knowledge source version in the bases the record owns or selects: verdict, closed signal codes, the result id a release names, whether it is quarantined and who released it. Content-free, never a quote. The release reason is member-written, so it is shown to owners and admins only. Empty when nothing was screened.

post.summary: Release quarantined material so a run may use it
post.description: Lets one screening result's text through despite its verdict, with a reason of 1 to 500 characters that is never candidate material. Owners and admins only, or the owner token. Only a record's own results are released (404 otherwise); a result that a newer one replaced answers 409 result_superseded, and a clear one 409 not_releasable. Releasing a result again returns its release. The release covers that result only: a later flagged or unscreened result quarantines the text again.

reason.description: Why the text is let through: a short note, never candidate material.

patch.summary: Change a workspace's author and critic models
patch.description: Applies from the next run; recorded runs keep the pair they ran with. Only Anthropic and OpenAI models are routed. A pair from one lineage answers 422 unless a reason is given, and a change while a run is executing answers 422.

independenceOverrideRationale.description: Required only when the author and critic descend from the same weights.

put.summary: Select the knowledge bases a workspace's runs use
put.description: Replaces the selection; it applies from the next run. Each knowledge base must be ready: active, with at least one source and every source's file held. A base without a source answers 422 `knowledge_base_empty`.

combinationApproved.description: Required to combine several knowledge bases in one workspace's runs.

put.description: Saves the text as a new version and makes it the policy the workspace's next runs follow. Setting the same text again keeps its version.

content.description: The policy as Markdown; at most 64 KiB once encoded as UTF-8.

get.summary: Read a workspace's active writing policy
Read the writing policy template
get.description: The policy a new desktop workspace starts with, for an editor to begin from when a workspace has none. Reading it saves nothing.

get.summary: List a workspace's writing policy versions, without their text
Estimate the credits a run on the workspace's settings would reserve
get.description: Prices the workspace as it is now, the way starting a run does: the application's own model pair when `applicationId` names one with a pair, otherwise the workspace's configured models, at its round limit. Refuses nothing. In sign-in mode a member also gets `plan` (whether the plan allows the tiers, with the code and the role and tier the run start would refuse with) and `balance` (whether `remaining` covers the estimate). A model whose tier cannot be determined cannot be priced and answers 422 `model_tier_unknown`.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Price a run on this application, whose own model pair applies.

post.summary: Create a job brief from pasted sources
post.description: Saves the brief, then screens each source for prompt injection. The answer's screening shows each source's verdict and signal codes, never a quote; a flagged or unscreened source is quarantined and a run on the brief is refused (409 material_quarantined) until an owner or admin releases it. Absent when screening is off. In a live workspace, a brief made from an application's job text is saved without extraction; once screening clears that text, the worker extracts it and saves the next draft version, and the answer's extraction says pending.

get.summary: Read a job brief, latest or at one version

patch.summary: Edit a job brief, saving a new draft version
patch.description: Replaces the patch's fields on the latest version and saves the result as a new draft. A stale expectedVersion answers 409, so an edit never overwrites one the client has not seen.

get.summary: List a job brief's versions, oldest first

post.summary: Mark a job brief version as reviewed

get.summary: List a workspace's job applications, the default one first

post.summary: Create a job application from a pasted job description
post.description: Keeps the text with the application. Its job brief is then created from that text, as a separate step, so the requirements can be extracted and reviewed.

jobText.description: The pasted job description, kept with the application.

get.summary: Read one job application

patch.summary: Rename, archive or restore a job application

archived.description: True archives the application, false restores it.

post.summary: Begin a run; a worker executes it
post.description: Persists the run and its context without calling a provider, then queues it for a worker. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same run and queues it again if it is not already waiting. In sign-in mode the candidate record needs a current provider transmission consent naming every provider the workspace's models use (409 transmission_consent_required). A run on a brief whose job source, or on a knowledge source the workspace selects, is quarantined by injection screening and not released answers 409 material_quarantined and lists the stored results to release. With screening on, a run on material that has no stored screening result, such as a brief saved while screening was off or whose result failed to save, answers 409 material_unscreened and lists the brief sources and knowledge source versions to screen by ids only; save the brief again or upload the file again to screen it. In sign-in mode the organisation's plan then has to allow the run: 403 plan_required without a plan, 422 model_tier_unknown when a model's tier cannot be determined, 403 model_tier_not_in_plan (with role and tier) for a tier the plan lacks, 429 run_cap_reached (with cap and limit) at the plan's concurrent or daily run cap, and 402 credits_insufficient (with estimate and remaining) when the balance does not cover the run's estimate. The estimate is reserved before the run is saved; a retry with the same Idempotency-Key reserves nothing more, and a run that cannot be saved gives its credits back.

modelProfiles.description: Exact author and critic profile versions bound to this run, such as a preset's pair; their models replace the workspace's for this run. Without them the run uses provider-default runtime controls and unknown context windows.

candidateProfile.description: A reviewed career profile version bound to this run, as the shared screens choose it. It must be bound to the workspace's current knowledge selection.

get.summary: Read a run's state
List every career profile version of a workspace
get.description: Every saved version of every profile, oldest first per profile: the shared screens build the reviewed-profile catalog a run chooses from out of it.

get.summary: Read a career profile, latest or at one version

patch.summary: Edit a career profile, saving a new draft version
patch.description: Replaces the latest version's facts or issues and saves the result as a new draft. A stale expectedVersion answers 409.
The facts and issues that replace the latest version's; nothing else is editable.

get.summary: List a career profile's versions

post.summary: Mark a career profile's latest draft reviewed
post.description: Saves the latest draft as a reviewed version, which a run can then bind. A stale expectedVersion, or a latest version that is not a draft, answers 409; open issues answer 422 profile_rule until each is acknowledged or resolved.

get.summary: Say whether a career profile is current with the career evidence

post.summary: Derive a career profile from the workspace's selected evidence
post.description: Queues the derivation for a worker, which saves the next profile version; poll the derivation for its progress and outcome. A fixture workspace calls no model. One derivation runs per profile at a time: another answers 409 derivation_running. In sign-in mode the candidate record needs a current provider transmission consent (409 transmission_consent_required).

providerDataApproved.description: The person approved sending the selected career evidence to the workspace's author company. Without it, a live workspace's derivation is refused.

fullExtraction.description: Extract every source again instead of only new or changed ones.

get.summary: Read where a career profile's newest derivation stands

delete.summary: Cancel a career profile's waiting or running derivation
delete.description: A running derivation stops before its next provider call and saves no version. cancelled is false when none was waiting or running.

get.summary: List the models and presets the hosted service runs

put.summary: Set or clear a job application's model pair
put.description: Exact author and critic model profile versions from two different companies, for the application's new runs. The default application always uses the workspace's pair.

modelProfiles.description: The pair for this application's new runs; null uses the workspace's pair again.

put.summary: Choose the run whose draft a job application uses

get.summary: Read the job description a job application keeps
Read a run's review: the draft, its findings and its readiness

put.summary: Decide a finding of the run's current draft
put.description: Records the owner's decision on one finding, by the id the review gives it. Only a run awaiting approval takes decisions (409 review_closed otherwise); the latest decision for a finding wins.

put.summary: Edit a block of the run's current draft
put.description: Records the owner's replacement text for one block. The review shows the latest edit in place of the draft's text. Only a run awaiting approval takes edits (409 review_closed otherwise).

post.summary: Approve the run's current draft
post.description: Approves a run awaiting approval after its independent critic review. A blocking finding still pending, deferred or merely accepted answers 409 findings_unresolved, as on the desktop. When the final CV checks fail, it answers 409 readiness_blocked and the review's approvalCheck lists the blockers; approving past them needs readinessOverrideRationale.

readinessOverrideRationale.description: Required only when the final CV checks fail; recorded with the approval.

post.summary: Stop the run for good
post.description: Stops a run that is not finished; a stopped run is never resumed. Stopping it again answers the stopped run.

post.summary: Ask for another round; a worker drafts it
post.description: Moves a run awaiting approval to revising, with the owner's optional direction for the author, then queues it. The API runs no model call. The round and budget limits apply (409 run_state_conflict). A retry with the same Idempotency-Key answers the same run and queues it again if needed. In sign-in mode the candidate record needs a current provider transmission consent naming every provider the workspace's models use (409 transmission_consent_required).

candidateDirection.description: The owner's short direction for the next round's author, never career evidence.

post.summary: Pause an active run
post.description: Pauses a run that is drafting, reviewing or revising. A step already running finishes, and the worker leaves the run until the owner resumes it.

post.summary: Resume a paused run; a worker continues it
post.description: Lifts the owner's pause without running a step, then queues the run so a worker continues from its current step. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key answers the same run and queues it again if needed. In sign-in mode the candidate record needs a current provider transmission consent naming every provider the workspace's models use (409 transmission_consent_required).

get.summary: Read the review state the shared screens open on
get.description: The run on screen with its draft, findings, decisions and edits, the workspace's readiness for the next run, and what a live run sends to which provider. Without a run it is the workspace's start state, with `runId` `pending`.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: The job application to show; its newest run when no run is named.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: The run to show; the workspace's or the application's newest when absent.

post.summary: Export the approved draft as Markdown, DOCX or PDF
post.description: Renders the approved draft, checks it, and stores the document with its checksum; the run becomes exported. A run not yet approved answers 409. PDFs come from the built-in writer. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key answers the same export.

templateId.description: A built-in rendering template, such as classic, modern or compact.

get.summary: List a run's exports, newest first
Download an exported document
get.description: Answers the document's bytes with its media type, as an attachment, and its SHA-256 in X-Content-SHA256. The bytes are checked against the export's recorded checksum first: a document that no longer matches answers 409 export_integrity and is never sent.

200.description: The document's bytes, in its media type.

schema.description: The document's bytes, in its media type.

get.summary: Read what a run used and cost, by company, model and route
Read the tenant's usage and estimated cost for a month

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: The UTC month, as YYYY-MM; calls count in the month they completed in.

post.summary: Create a knowledge base for candidate sources

workspaceId.description: The candidate record the base belongs to: required in sign-in mode, where only callers who reach the record reach the base. Owner-token mode keeps every base tenant-wide and ignores it.

get.summary: List the knowledge bases the caller can reach
get.description: With `workspaceId`, only the bases that candidate record owns, in both modes. Without it, owner-token mode lists every base of the tenant; in sign-in mode, owners and admins see every base, and a member sees the bases their assigned candidate records own.

parameters.name: workspaceId
parameters.description: In sign-in mode, only the bases this candidate record owns. Owner-token mode ignores it.

get.summary: List a knowledge base's sources with their latest file's metadata

post.summary: Upload a candidate source file
post.description: Send the file itself as the request body, with its media type as the Content-Type: application/pdf, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, text/markdown, text/plain. The type is checked against the file's signature; the file is stored, and its text is read only to screen it. In sign-in mode the base's candidate record needs a current material storage consent (409 storage_consent_required). The same bytes in the same knowledge base answer 200 with the existing source, so a retry is safe. After the file is stored its text is screened for prompt injection; the answer's screening shows the verdict and signal codes, never a quote. A flagged or unscreened file is quarantined: a run that would use it is refused (409 material_quarantined) until an owner or admin releases it.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The file's name, shown in source lists and evidence references.

get.summary: List a knowledge base's sensitivity rules

post.summary: Add a sensitivity rule to a knowledge base
post.description: Saves a new version of the rule list; it applies from the next run. A rule with the same id, or the same tier and match, is refused with 422.

tier.description: never-share sections never reach a provider; sensitive ones need the workspace's consent.

id.description: The rule's id; generated when absent.

delete.summary: Remove a sensitivity rule from a knowledge base
delete.description: Saves a new version of the rule list without the rule.

get.summary: Read a candidate record's consents: the current state and the history

post.summary: Record a consent grant or withdrawal for a candidate record
post.description: Entries are append-only: a withdrawal is a new entry. The recording member is the caller.

basis.description: Material storage takes any basis; provider transmission only the candidate's consent.

providers.description: Required on a provider transmission grant, and only there.

get.summary: Download everything held about a candidate record as a zip
get.description: Streams the record's archive (record archive v1): its manifest, its rows as JSON and the original bytes of its sources and exported documents. Owners and admins only. The manifest's SHA-256 is in X-Archive-Manifest-SHA256. A stored object that is missing or no longer matches its checksum answers 409 archive_integrity before anything is sent.

get.summary: Read who the caller is: the owner token or an organisation's member
List the members of the caller's organisation

post.summary: Invite a person to the caller's organisation by email
post.description: They become active on their first sign-in with that verified email. Active members and pending invitations both take a seat: 409 plan_limit_reached (limit seats) when the plan has none left, 403 plan_required when the organisation has no plan. Inviting an email already invited or active answers 409 member_exists and takes no seat.

patch.description: The organisation's last owner keeps the owner role.

delete.summary: Remove a member from the caller's organisation
delete.description: The organisation's last owner cannot be removed.

post.summary: Create an organisation and invite its first owner
post.description: Operator only: takes the deployment's owner token in both authentication modes, never a member's sign-in.

organisationId.description: Also the tenant id; it cannot change later.

get.summary: Read the organisation's plan, limits and credit balance
get.description: Any signed-in member may read it. `used` counts the period's allowance that finished runs settled and the part of `reserved` taken from it, so a started run counts at once. `warning` is true once `used` is at least 80% of `allowance`; it is never true on an unlimited plan or a zero allowance. An organisation with no plan answers 403 `plan_required`. Owner-token mode has no organisations: the route answers 404 there.

delete.summary: Delete the caller's organisation and everything it holds
delete.description: Owners only. Erases every candidate record as `DELETE /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}` does, then every object left under the tenant's storage prefix, then the tenant-wide knowledge bases, idempotency keys and the organisation with its members. The organisation id is typed back as `confirm` (400 `confirmation_mismatch`). A queued or running run anywhere in the organisation answers 409 `run_active`. The first call marks the organisation as closing, and from then on every member request but this one answers 409 `organisation_closing`. Calling again finishes an interrupted deletion. Accounts at the identity provider are not touched: a person's sign-in simply no longer resolves to an organisation.

confirm.description: The organisation id again, typed back by the person.

delete.summary: Delete an organisation and everything it holds
delete.description: Operator only: takes the deployment's owner token in both authentication modes. Erases every candidate record as `DELETE /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}` does, then every object left under the tenant's storage prefix, then the tenant-wide knowledge bases, idempotency keys and the organisation with its members. The organisation id is typed back as `confirm` (400 `confirmation_mismatch`). A queued or running run anywhere in the organisation answers 409 `run_active`. The first call marks the organisation as closing, and from then on every member request but this one answers 409 `organisation_closing`. Calling again finishes an interrupted deletion. Accounts at the identity provider are not touched: a person's sign-in simply no longer resolves to an organisation. The owner token's own tenant has no organisation in the directory; it is erased the same way, record by record, and a repeated call answers 204 again.

confirm.description: The organisation id again, typed back by the person.

put.description: Operator only: takes the deployment's owner token in both authentication modes. Replaces the organisation's plan assignment and appends it to its history. An unknown plan id, a seat-priced plan without seats, an invalid date or entitlements the plan cannot resolve answer 422 `invalid_plan_assignment`; an unknown organisation answers 404 `organisation_not_found`. Answers the assignment and the entitlements it resolves to.

planId.description: The plan's id in catalog v1: individual, job-search-pass, pro, team, business, internal. Anything else answers 422.

overrides.description: Per-organisation entitlement overrides, merged over the plan.

seats.description: Seats held; required for a seat-priced plan (team, business), ignored otherwise.

periodStart.description: The UTC date the credit period starts; today's date when omitted.

post.summary: Grant an organisation credits
post.description: Operator only: takes the deployment's owner token in both authentication modes. Adds credits that expire 12 months later and are spent after the plan's allowance. The reason is a short code, never free text. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key answers the first grant and balance without granting again; a key reused with another request answers 409 `idempotency_conflict`. An unknown organisation answers 404 `organisation_not_found`.

credits.description: Credits to add; they expire 12 months after the grant.

reason.description: A short content-free code such as `goodwill` or `support.2026-10`, never free text.

get.summary: Read an organisation's plan, entitlements and credit balance
get.description: Operator only: takes the deployment's owner token in both authentication modes. The assignment and entitlements are null while no plan is assigned. An unknown organisation answers 404 `organisation_not_found`.
